Blueprint {{ bpNum }}

One clinic, one flow

Clinozy shows the clinic as people moving through a visit. Staff act on the person in front of them; the software carries details forward to the next step. Priority outcomes: no retyping between steps, the right person found in two seconds, every handoff visible, money and stock always correct.

A · Role-first workspace

Each role gets its own home.

Saves: no irrelevant screens.

Costs: handoffs hide between homes; people with two roles switch constantly; eight homes to build and teach.

B · Patient-and-visit workspace

Everything happens inside one person’s visit.

Saves: context switching; nothing retyped.

Costs: no overview of the day; pharmacy, stock and accounts are not patient-shaped.

C · Work-queue-first

Staff clear a prioritised list of tasks.

Saves: nothing is forgotten; owners and due times are explicit.

Costs: live visits feel like tickets; new staff struggle to see the bigger picture.

Recommendation: hybrid of B and C, with roles as lenses

Today is a flow of live visits (C for the day) with a work queue beside it for everything not in the building.

The visit sheet (B) opens over Today for consult, session, checkout. One person, one sheet, many records.

Roles highlight columns and pick the starting room. People covering two roles tick both; no switching.

Rooms in the bottom dock hold work that is not visit-shaped: pharmacy, stock, money, insights.

Discovery: every card shows its one next action as a labelled button. Speed: / search, number keys for rooms, Esc back. Scale: a solo clinic hides empty columns; a chain filters by branch; other specialties rename stages and treatment templates, not the product.

How the shell works

Header: logo · All sections (compass, pin to bar) · pinned tabs (collapse into More ⌄) · ⌘K search · branch picker (hidden with one branch) · account.

One colour per section, shown on nav tabs, the sections list, the square before each title, drawer step numbers and the access grid. Branches carry their own colour.

Roles add up. A user holds one or more roles (Dr. Nisha = Doctor + Admin). Access is the union: View / Create / Edit / Delete per section plus special permissions (bill below offer price, see lowest price, close the day, reverse settled payments, export, change roles). Admin is always full.

Without View a section disappears from the header and search; without Create the New… buttons go; without Edit records open read-only; without Delete every red action is gone. Preview as role runs the whole app with that access.

Branches: address, hours, GSTIN, team and default doctor / desk / therapist / pharmacist. Records that belong to a branch carry a Branch chip defaulting to the header branch; offerings and offers pick where they are available.

Shared patterns

A · Lists. Sticky uppercase header, sortable, 3px status edge. Columns fold into a metadata line when the width is short (Show all ↔ Fit to width). Search collapses to an icon and debounces 300 ms; every fetch shows a skeleton with short, varied bars. Row actions are direct icon buttons with a dark tooltip; three or more float over the row on hover so they take no column. Delete is last, red, after a divider, and always asks for a reason in a drawer.

B · Filters. One popover per list: Created and Follow-up date sections everywhere, coloured chips per column, Apply filter = a fetch, one joined × clears all. Column show/hide is a plain, uncoloured dropdown.

C · Drawers. Everything that is a form, confirm or detail is a right drawer (560 / 680 / 840 / 1040). Numbered steps with a peek grid when collapsed; the last field of each row stretches; pickers stay half width, short options a third. Save goes through apiSave: “Saving…”, and on failure the draft stays with “Not saved · your changes are kept”.

D · Dropdowns. One engine for every picker: floating popup, search for dynamic data, coloured options, Recent picks, “Add ‘query’” quick create and “New … — full details” that opens the record’s drawer stacked on top. Dates and times are dropdowns too; phones are digits with +91 stored as one string.

E · People. Any patient, lead, Medical contact or teammate renders as a chip; hovering fetches first, then shows one contact card positioned around the chip. Opening a person goes to the patient file or the lead drawer — there is no separate profile screen.

F · Money. One invoice drawer for clinic, consultation and Medical sales; offers pre-apply as discount; the hidden lowest price blocks over-discounting with “ask an admin”. One Payments ledger for everything — Received against any invoice, Paid against supplier bills (Medical and Clinic stock POs) or other spend — with split modes, editable until Day close, then only reversible through a credit note. Medical › Payments is the same ledger filtered to Medical. Day close opens with the opening cash to accept (stamped with who and when), then the count, then a closed-day report of what happened.

G · Documents. Prescription and invoice print as A4 sheets measured from the clinic’s samples; every Rx / invoice row, drawer and viewer has Print next to Preview.

H · Tasks. Never typed in: rules derive them (unreplied messages, follow-ups, claims, confirmations, no-shows, feedback, aftercare, next visit not set, regulars gone quiet). Outcomes change the record and the task closes itself.

I · Feel. Popovers fade in 160 ms from their anchored corner; drawers slide 340 ms; buttons ignore a repeat click for 450 ms; thin custom scrollbars with a stable gutter so content never shifts; no gradients, no centred modals, no emoji.

Journeys 1–5

1 · WhatsApp enquiry → booking
Trigger → message arrives; card appears in Enquiries.
Context → chat, source ad, phone match.
Actions → Book · resolve match · pick slot · Book & send.
System → lead created with source; slots check doctor, room, machine; recheck on commit; confirm task.
Feedback → “Rechecking…” then confirmed note.
Done → card leaves Enquiries; chat stays on person.
Recovery → slot taken: next one offered; send fails: queued + retry.
2 · Returning patient → check-in
Trigger → arrives at desk.
Context → Arriving column, or / search.
Actions → Check in (1 tap), or search 3–4 characters and pick.
System → visit starts; pack and dues attach; doctor queue updated.
Feedback → toast with Undo.
Done → card in Waiting.
Recovery → wrong person: Undo; walk-in: search → New visit.
3 · Consult → prescription
Trigger → doctor opens consult.
Context → history, allergies, photos beside the note.
Actions → dictate or type · copy last Rx · review each line · Approve·print·send.
System → note saved as draft until signed; Rx sent with exact items to pharmacy.
Feedback → per-line “Review” turns to “✓ Reviewed”.
Done → card moves to treatment or checkout.
Recovery → drafts autosave; AI down: type as usual.
4 · Treatment → session → follow-up
Trigger → therapist opens session.
Context → pack progress, instructions, last settings, photos.
Actions → adjust settings · areas · capture · Complete.
System → one session used, exactly once; feedback task created.
Feedback → “Session 4 recorded · 2 left”.
Done → card to checkout.
Recovery → reverse with reason; session restored with audit entry.
5 · Billing → payment → receipt
Trigger → Checkout on card.
Context → services from visit, pack cover, dues, advance.
Actions → Create bill · choose mode · Receive.
System → server totals; discount before GST; FY numbering.
Feedback → receipt number only after server confirms.
Done → receipt printed and on WhatsApp.
Recovery → finalised bills change by cancel or credit note; partial → due + reminder.

Journeys 6–10

6 · Prescription → pharmacy sale
Trigger → approved Rx appears in queue.
Context → lines, stock, batches.
Actions → confirm batches (preset) · decide unavailable line · Complete sale.
System → earliest valid expiry picked; expired blocked; price ≤ MRP; stock reduced per batch.
Feedback → “Completing…” then sale number.
Done → bill printed; card leaves flow.
Recovery → returns reverse money and batch stock together.
7 · Purchase → receipt → stock
Trigger → delivery with invoice.
Context → open PO lines.
Actions → enter received, free, batch, expiry per line · Post.
System → pack→unit conversion shown; short lines stay open; payable created.
Feedback → flags for near-expiry and shortfall.
Done → stock and supplier balance updated.
Recovery → posted receipts corrected by return-to-supplier, not edits.
8 · Follow-up → outcome
Trigger → task due.
Context → reason, owner, last contact.
Actions → call or message · tap outcome.
System → configured next step runs (retry, rebook, escalate) and is shown.
Feedback → result line on the task, Undo.
Done → task closed.
Recovery → escalation reassigns owner visibly.
9 · Owner question → records
Trigger → owner opens Insights.
Context → five totals, each with a written definition.
Actions → click a total · open a record.
System → filters carried into the list.
Feedback → breadcrumb of filters.
Done → owner sees the bills behind the number.
Recovery → slow report: background export, notification.
10 · Import → reconcile → go-live
Trigger → trial import.
Context → counts, money, stock side by side.
Actions → resolve each mismatch · owner signs off.
System → sign-off locked until exact match.
Feedback → open checks count.
Done → final import, go-live.
Recovery → old app read-only 90 days; rerun trial any time.

Rules and states

Appointments. Slots offered only when person, room and machine are all free inside branch hours and holidays. Rechecked on Book. Reschedule moves reminders; cancel removes pending ones.

People. Phone is never treated as identity. Matches ask “same person / family member / decide later”. Data, photo and marketing consent are separate. Photo location data stripped on upload.

Money. Server calculates totals. Discount before tax. Old bills keep old prices. Finalised bills: cancel or credit note only. Payments are never edited.

Stock. No negative stock. Expired batches cannot be chosen. Every movement tied to item and batch. Price ≤ MRP. Returns reverse money and stock together.

Messaging. Sending, sent, delivered, read, not delivered, queued. Retry and SMS fallback shown on the message. Opt-outs block campaigns. Provider outage shows a banner; clinic work continues.

Repeated submission. Commit buttons switch to “Completing…” and ignore further presses; each request carries a one-time key so the server records it once.

Concurrent staff. Cards update live. If a record changed since you opened it, a note says who changed what and offers “Load latest”; your unsaved input is kept.

Stale data. Lists show “Updated 10:42”. Slots, stock and totals are always rechecked on commit.

Loading. Layout appears at once with quiet placeholders in the same shapes. Exports run in the background.

Errors. Stated in plain words next to the field or button, with the next step. Nothing entered is lost.

Permissions. Restricted sections show “Only doctors can see clinical notes” rather than disappearing.

Interruptions. Drafts autosave per person. Coming back reopens the same sheet and tab. Session timeout keeps drafts for re-login.

Optimistic only when reversible. Check-in, task outcomes and moving cards update instantly with Undo. Bookings, payments, stock and approvals wait for the server.

AI, visuals and access

Phase one is assistance only: drafts that a person reads and sends or signs. Agents that act alone come later, one at a time, after launch approval.

AssistTrigger and contextWhat appearsAutomaticNeeds approvalIf unavailable or unsure
Enquiry replyNew message · chat, prices, free slotsDraft in composerNothingSendingEmpty composer; medical question → handed to person
Conversation summaryOpening a long thread3-line summaryShown, not stored—Full thread only
Dictated noteDoctor presses DictateDashed draft in noteDraft savedSigningTyping; unclear words marked
After-care messageSession completed · template, languageReview itemNothingSendingPlain approved template
Owner questionTyped question · permitted recordsAnswer + link to recordsRead-only query—“Can’t answer reliably” + report link
Template draftingAdmin asks in SettingsDraft templateNothingPublishingWrite manually
AI rules
No diagnosis or clinical approval by AI. Drafts marked until approved. Same permissions and audit as people. Minimum data sent; names masked where possible. Per-feature switches, usage limits, patient opt-out. Sending is marked as cannot-be-undone. Later: Rx assist, photo sorting, invoice reading, agents for follow-up, booking, collections, stock.
Visual and accessibility
Calm paper ground, serif headings, pastel stage colours (lavender enquiry, sky arriving, butter waiting and money, blush clinical, sage treatment, mint pharmacy). Colour always paired with a text label. Visible focus ring, full keyboard path, 44 px touch targets on tablet and phone, labelled fields, errors announced. ₹ with Indian grouping, IST default, one date format per clinic. WCAG 2.2 AA is the target; compliance to be confirmed by testing.

Release and testing

0Decisions and design · settle the open decisions list. 1Foundations · search, person band, history, work queue, permissions, audit. Pull forward: minimal service list with durations and prices; branch hours. 2Leads, calendar, tasks, messaging · Today flow up to Waiting. 3Patients, clinical, treatments, photos. Pull forward: package definition and session counter (no pricing) so sessions can be counted. 4Services, packages, billing, payments · Checkout tab. 5Inventory and pharmacy. Before this, Rx lines use a medicine master shared with stock. 6Insights and first AI drafts. 7Move-in and switch-over. +After go-live: agents one at a time, each with its own approval.

Dependencies to watch: booking needs durations (phase 4 data); sessions need pack definitions; pharmacy handoff needs a medicine master; dues on the person band need billing; migration needs every record type finished.

Usability test plan

Participants: 2 front desk, 2 doctors, 2 therapists, 1 counsellor, 1 pharmacist, 1 accountant, 1 owner, from 3 clinics of different size. Tablet and a mid-range phone on 4G included.

Tasks: book a WhatsApp lead; check in a family member who shares a phone; repeat a prescription; complete a session and fix a wrong one; take a partial payment; dispense with one item out of stock; receive a short delivery; find why collections fell.

Measure: time, errors, wrong-person picks, hesitations, number of screens, confidence (1–5). Run with interruptions: a phone call mid-task.

Pass: 8 of 10 complete each task unaided within the target; zero duplicate payments or sessions.
